newsitem.title: ITALY: Incentive leads Italians to scrap 139,000 cars.
newsitem.headline: Incentive leads Italians to scrap 139,000 cars.

text.p: Italians have sent nearly 139,000 cars to the scrapyard since the government brought in incentives to encourage motorists to trade in old cars for new, the country's main automobile club ACI said on Saturday.

It said the figure corresponded to the number of cars removed from Italy's vehicle register in the first three months of 1997. The ACI statement gave no comparative figure for the first quarter of 1996.
It said 29,227 new cars had been registered in place of scrapped cars, a difference it attributed to regulations that give Italian 60 days to submit their application.
In January the government introduced cash incentives for car owners to scrap vehicles over 10 years old and buy new ones in a scheme to boost flagging domestic sales.
Under the scheme, which will last until the end of September, car makers have to match each government bonus on offer with a discount for the same amount.
Italy's Fiat, the domestic market leader, has forecast total extra car sales of some 300,000, half of which would be Fiat group vehicles, as a result of the incentives.
